title: Bond Market Reckoning: Why Your Money Is Next | Tavi Costa
speaker: Tavi Costa (Azuria Capital), host David Lin

macro_themes.theme: Inflate the way out of debt
macro_themes.view: 75-80% chance policymakers inflate their way out of the debt problem rather than accept a 2008-style deflationary shock; hard assets the big beneficiaries.
Expects politicians and the Treasury (bigger buybacks, front-end issuance, possible yield curve control) to move to suppress yields within 6-12 months, which would be very bullish for metals.
Both US stocks and bonds are expensive, but rising yields make bonds increasingly attractive relative to equities; gradually rotate from equities to bonds.

macro_themes.theme: Rotation to emerging markets and resources
macro_themes.view: Money is rotating to emerging/Latin American markets and the resource space; US tech remains over-owned with room for the rotation to run for a decade.
Dollar weakening and yield suppression will mark the next decade.

calls.reason: Big move up, consolidation, sentiment 'in the toilet'; supply imbalance large; silver to lead gold and outperform over 6-12 months. Base case back to $80s-90s, flirting with $100, then re-establishing triple digits and revisiting this year's ~$120 high. $300 in 6 months possible but not base case.
calls.quote: I think we're going to see triple digits on silver again and and it's going to establish itself at that level eventually here.

calls.condition: Significant return in gold prices if yields find some ground
calls.reason: Gold ~25% off the $5,500 high; inflation/debt/valuation 'trifecta' extremely bullish; secular bull market where gold could reach $15-30k one day.
calls.quote: I really think gold is is is still extremely uh attractive at these prices... I'm very bullish gold

calls.reason: Miners at record margins with strong balance sheets, priced by analysts as if gold returns to ~$3,000-3,500; an arbitrage on higher metal prices. Silver companies are his biggest exposure (new Azuria mining fund >50% silver).
calls.quote: the miners are exceptionally cheap for the next 5 to 10 years because they are priced as if gold prices will go back to 3,000

calls.reason: Oil above $100; he redeployed most oil capital into metals and mining and expects some consolidation in the oil space, though he keeps some US oil-service names that should benefit from higher activity.
calls.quote: I think that would be normal to see some sort of uh um consolidation in the oil space again.

calls.reason: Yields near levels where bonds become attractive (10y real yield approaching 3% vs S&P earnings yield ~3.5-3.7%); expects intervention to suppress yields over the next 6-12 months. Bearish yield = bullish bonds.
calls.quote: I think you're getting close to it.

calls.reason: US equities expensive on every metric (CAPE, P/E, market cap/GDP) and earnings growth unlikely to stay as strong; expects relative underperformance vs bonds, metals and emerging markets over the next couple of years.
calls.quote: you want to be rotating out of both markets... starting to relocate capital from equity markets to uh the bond market

notes: Recorded Monday Oct 12, 2026 (host says so); listing approx_date 2026-10-13 is off by a day. No short-term levels given; long-horizon macro views only. Gold $15-30k is a 'one day' secular figure, recorded as long-term target 15000 (lower end). Silver price ~$60 inferred from 'at 60 bucks'.
